newsitem.title: INDIA: Approaching India cyclone threatens rice crop.
newsitem.headline: Approaching India cyclone threatens rice crop.

text.p: A powerful cyclone off India's southeastern Andhra Pradesh state could affect rice crops if it crosses the coast but oilseeds are not grown in the likely area of impact, state officials and experts said on Thursday.
In their latest report, weathermen said the cyclone had weakened and was now seen moving away slightly from the coast.
"It has weakened temporarily and moved slightly away. But the danger persists," said J.V.M. Naidu, head of the cyclone warning centre at Visakhapatna, in southern Andhra Pradesh.
State relief commissioner Harishankar Brahma told Reuters: "If there are heavy rains and winds, the rice crop in Guntoor, Krishna, and Ongole will be affected.
"But the oilseeds crop will not be affected as is is not grown in these areas," he added.
The Guntoor, Krishna and Ongole coastal areas contribute a total of around 20 percent of the state's rice production.
"Most of the rice...crop has been harvested," S.M. Virmani, from the International Crops Reasearch Institute for Semi-Arid Crops, based in the state capital, Hyderabad, said.
"But some of the crop which may be lying in the fields for threshing and drying up will be damaged if there are heavy rains," he added.
A cyclone lashed coastal areas of Andhra Pradesh on November 6 and 7, killing 971 people and destroying a standing rice crop covering 435,000 hectares.
